question: Who among the following is a Jnanpith Award-winning woman writer?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahadevi Verma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahadevi Verma** was one of the most eminent writers of Hindi literature and a recipient of the prestigious **Jnanpith Award** in **1982**.
 
• She is widely regarded as a pioneer in modern Hindi literature and is considered one of the four pillars of Chhayavad poetry, alongside **Suryakant Tripathi 'Nirala,' Jai Shankar Prasad, and Sumitranandan Pant**.
 
• Her works often reflect themes of **feminism, individualism, and the human struggle**. She was known for her contributions to both poetry and prose.
 
• Mahadevi Verma's most famous works include **"Yama" (a poetry collection that won the Jnanpith Award)** and prose writings such as **"Aatmika" and "Smriti Ki Rekhayen."**
 
• She also earned the title of **"Modern Meera"** due to her spiritual and deeply emotional style of writing, which resonated with readers across generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jnanpith Award:**

 
 
• The **Jnanpith Award** is one of India's highest literary honors, established in **1961** by the Bharatiya Jnanpith organization.
 
• It is awarded annually to an author for their outstanding contribution to literature in any of the **22 official languages** of India as per the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
 
• Recipients of the award are presented with a **citation, a shawl, and a cash prize**.
 
• The first recipient of the Jnanpith Award was **G. Sankara Kurup** in **Malayalam**. Mahadevi Verma became the first woman recipient of this award for her contributions in **Hindi literature**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Sarojini Naidu:** Known as the **"Nightingale of India"**, Sarojini Naidu was a poet and freedom fighter. Although she made significant contributions to Indian literature, she did not receive the Jnanpith Award.
 
• **Kamala Surayya:** Also known as **Kamala Das**, she was a renowned poet and writer who contributed to Malayalam and English literature. She received several awards but did not win the Jnanpith Award.
 
• **Subhadra Kumari Chauhan:** A famous Hindi poet known for her patriotic works such as **"Jhansi Ki Rani"**, Subhadra Kumari Chauhan did not receive the Jnanpith Award.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Mahadevi Verma's Work:**
 
 
• Her work is celebrated for its **lyrical beauty and depth**, often exploring themes of social reform, human emotions, and spirituality.
 
• She was also a strong advocate for **women’s rights** and often addressed issues of gender inequality in her writings.
 
• Mahadevi Verma's influence on Hindi literature and the Chhayavad movement has been profound and enduring.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chhayavad Movement:**

 
 
• Chhayavad refers to the romanticism movement in Hindi literature, which emerged in the early 20th century.
 
• It is characterized by a focus on **nature, beauty, personal emotions, and spirituality**.
 
• Mahadevi Verma was one of the key figures in this movement, alongside Sumitranandan Pant, Jai Shankar Prasad, and Suryakant Tripathi 'Nirala'.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Mahadevi Verma:**
 
 
• She was awarded numerous accolades, including the **Padma Bhushan** and the **Sahitya Akademi Fellowship**.
 
• She served as the editor of **"Chand" magazine**, contributing significantly to Hindi journalism and literature.
 
• In recognition of her contributions, institutions and awards have been established in her name to promote Hindi literature.
